ORDER This miscellaneous appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is filed by the insurance company being aggrieved of award dated 31.07.2019 passed by the learned 14th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhopal in claim case No.1279/2016 (Mohd. Arhaan Vs.
Kripal Singh and another) on the ground that excessive amount has been awarded in favour of the claimants who lost both his parents in the accident.

3. Shri Ratnesh Kumar Yadav, learned counsel for the respondent No.1 supports the award.
4. After hearing learned counsel for the parties, perusal of record reveals that there are two income tax returns available on record.
One is for the assessment year 2014-2015 which was filed on 06.03.2016 (Ex.P-10) showing gross income of Tanvir Khan at Rs.2,25,000/-.
and another income tax return is for the assessment year 2015-2016, which was filed on 08.03.2016 showing gross total income at Rs.2,76,100/-.
Deductions under Chapter VI-A are same for both the years.

5. Thus, when these aspects are taken into consideration which are duly supported with evidence on record, it cannot be said that Tribunal has erred in making computation on the basis of admitted income tax returns.

There is no dispute as to the efficacy or correctness of these income tax returns and no such evidence was led by the insurance company to dispute them, therefore, in view of the available evidence, when award has been passed then that cannot be faulted with merely because higher amount of compensation will be payable by the insurance company.

6. In absence of any evidence to the contrary, impugned award cannot be disputed and, therefore,
appeal fails and is dismissed.
7. Record of the learned claims Tribunal be sent back.
